member.summary: Represents a 3D cone defined by an apex point, a base center, and a base radius. The cone's axis runs from the apex to the base center.

member.summary: The apex (tip) of the cone.

member.name: F:XEngine.Vector.Cone.BaseCenter
member.summary: The center of the base circle.

member.name: F:XEngine.Vector.Cone.BaseRadius
member.summary: The radius of the base circle.

member.name: M:XEngine.Vector.Cone.#ctor(XEngine.Vector.Float3,XEngine.Vector.Float3,System.Single)
member.summary: Initializes a new cone with the specified apex, base center, and base radius.
member.param: The center of the base circle.
The radius of the base circle.

member.summary: Initializes a new cone with the specified apex, base center, base radius using individual coordinate components.

member.summary: Gets the height of the cone (distance from apex to base).

member.summary: Gets the volume of the cone.

member.summary: Gets the lateral surface area of the cone (excluding the base).

member.summary: Gets the total surface area of the cone (including the base).

member.summary: Creates a cone from an apex, axis direction, height, and base radius.

member.name: T:XEngine.Vector.Geometry.CSGScene
member.summary:
An incremental N-ary CSG scene built from convex brushes (after Sander van Rossen's Realtime-CSG model). Brushes form an ordered list; later brushes override earlier ones where they overlap, so the final solid is "the last brush whose volume contains a point decides whether it is solid".
Each brush only interacts with brushes it spatially overlaps, so adding, moving, re-ordering, or removing one brush re-evaluates only that brush and the ones it touches; everything else keeps its cached surface. Overlap queries go through a broadphase so large scenes stay cheap to edit.
Every brush MUST be a convex closed solid. Build a concave shape from several brushes. Vertex, edge, loop, and face attributes are carried through; where two brushes define an attribute of the same name, the earlier brush's schema wins.
Each face is partitioned exactly (no gaps or overlaps). By default a T-junction welding pass makes the output watertight where independent cuts subdivide a shared face; disable it via for raw, faster output.

member.name: T:XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryCSG
member.summary:
CSG (Constructive Solid Geometry) operations for .
This is a polygon-based, plane-driven implementation (after Sander van Rossen's Realtime-CSG): each input solid is reduced to its set of face planes, rebuilt into a clean convex half-edge mesh, and booleaned by splitting polygons against the other solid's planes and categorizing the pieces as inside/outside/aligned. No triangulation is involved, so coplanar faces stay aligned and the output is clean n-gon geometry.
Attributes (vertex, edge, loop, and face) are carried through: every output polygon is traced back to the source face it lies on, and per-corner/per-vertex values are reconstructed by interpolating that source face at the output vertex's position. Where both inputs define an attribute of the same name, the schema of meshA wins.
IMPORTANT: Both inputs MUST be convex closed solids. A solid is treated purely as the intersection of the half-spaces behind its (outward-facing) face planes; concave geometry is not representable this way and will produce incorrect results. Face windings must be consistent so that face normals point outward.

member.summary: Computes the union of two convex solids.

member.summary: Computes the intersection of two convex solids.

All loop attributes (including UVs) are preserved on the resulting triangles. Faces that are already triangles are left unchanged. Modifies the mesh in-place.

member.name: M:XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryOperators.ExtrudeFaces(XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryData,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryData.Face},System.Single,XEngine.Vector.Geometry.ExtrudeMode)
member.summary: Extrude a collection of faces outward (or inward) along their normals. Creates new geometry by duplicating the faces and connecting them with wall faces.
member.param: The extrusion distance (positive = outward along normal, negative = inward).

The extrusion mode: AlongNormals - vertices move along averaged normals (shared vertices), AverageNormal - all vertices move along average of all face normals (shared vertices), PerFace - each face gets its own vertices (no sharing).

member.summary: Inset a collection of faces by shrinking them towards their centers. Creates new smaller faces and connects them with wall faces to the original edges.

member.name: M:XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryOperators.WeldVertices(XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryData,System.Single)
member.summary: Weld vertices that are within a distance threshold, merging them into single vertices. This is useful for cleaning up geometry with duplicate or nearly-duplicate vertices. Attributes are averaged based on the merged vertices.
member.param: The mesh to weld vertices in.
Maximum distance between vertices to be welded together.
member.returns: The number of vertices that were welded (removed).

member.name: M:XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryOperators.WeldVerticesAtPositions(XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryData,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{XEngine.Vector.Float3},System.Single)
member.summary: Weld vertices at specific positions by merging all vertices within threshold distance of each target. This is useful for welding specific problem areas without affecting the entire mesh.
member.param: The mesh to weld vertices in.
Positions around which to weld vertices.
Maximum distance from target positions to weld vertices.
member.returns: The number of vertices that were welded (removed).

member.name: M:XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryOperators.BevelVertices(XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryData,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{XEngine.Vector.Geometry.GeometryData.Vertex},System.Single)

member.name: M:XEngine.Vector.Geometry.Intersection.PolygonMeanValueWeights(XEngine.Vector.Float3,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{XEngine.Vector.Float3},System.Single[])
member.summary: Computes generalized barycentric coordinates of a point with respect to a planar polygon using Mean Value Coordinates (Floater 2003). The weights form a partition of unity (sum to 1) and reproduce the polygon's vertices, so they can interpolate any per-vertex quantity. The point is inside the polygon when every weight is non-negative; weights may be negative for points outside, which makes this usable as a containment test as well.
member.param: The query point, assumed to lie on (or close to) the polygon's plane.
The polygon's ordered vertices (convex or concave, 3 or more).
Output weights, one per polygon vertex; length must be at least polygon.Count.
member.returns: False if the polygon is degenerate or the weights buffer is too small.

member.name: T:XEngine.Vector.Spatial.DynamicBvh`1
member.summary:
A dynamic bounding-volume hierarchy for sets that change every frame (moving physics bodies, etc.). Leaves are inserted, removed, and moved individually with incremental tree rotations instead of a full rebuild.
Each leaf is stored with a fattened AABB (its tight bounds enlarged by ). While an object moves inside its fat box nothing in the tree changes, so small per-frame motion is nearly free; a re-insertion only happens once the object leaves its margin. Optionally the fat box can be extended along the object's motion to anticipate travel.
Items are referenced by a stable integer proxy id returned from . Overlap and ray queries are conservative (they test the fat boxes), so callers should do an exact narrow-phase test on the returned items.
member.typeparam: The item type stored at each leaf.

member.name: P:XEngine.Vector.Spatial.DynamicBvh`1.Margin
member.summary: Amount each leaf's bounds are enlarged on every side. Movement within this margin is free.

member.name: P:XEngine.Vector.Spatial.DynamicBvh`1.PredictionMultiplier
member.summary: When updating with a displacement, how far ahead along the motion the fat box is extended.
